title: Senior Digital Producer
content: The BBC Media Action office in Nigeria is seeking a Senior Digital Producer to lead the design and production of a digital strategy and content stream for a multi-component Social and Behaviour Change Communication (SBCC) programme focused on reproductive health and child spacing in Northern Nigeria. The Senior Digital Producer will utilise their editorial knowledge and digital skills to oversee the production of high-quality and impactful digital outputs across platforms. The role will hold responsibility for extending storytelling from TV/radio formats into digital, social media, and interactive formats.

title: Impact & Insights Officer
content:
Media Development Investment Fund (MDIF) is seeking an Impact & Insights Officer to help measure, understand and communicate the impact of our global investments across public interest information companies.

This role sits at the intersection of data analysis, monitoring & evaluation (MEL / M&E), and strategic insight. You will play a key role in transforming data into clear, compelling narratives that support decision-making, strengthen impact, and demonstrate value to donors, investors, and stakeholders.

If you believe in data as a force for good and are passionate about using insights to support independent media and information businesses worldwide, we encourage you to apply.

title: Director, Global Amplify Programs
content:
Media Development Investment Fund (MDIF) is the only not-for-profit impact investment fund dedicated to supporting independent media and information ventures. For over 30 years, we have provided financing and strategic support to news outlets and other information sources operating in some of the world’s most challenging environments, helping them grow, remain independent, and give people the information they need to build free, thriving societies. Media Advisory Services (MAS), MDIF’s in-house technical assistance arm, has delivered more than $35 million in media management advice across hundreds of interventions worldwide over 25 years.

MDIF’s flagship Amplify program is a global incubation and accelerator initiative supporting media entrepreneurs building sustainable, independent news and information businesses across Africa, Asia, Central & Eastern Europe, and Latin America.

title: Program Editor
content:
Al Jazeera English is an award-winning 24-hour international news channel providing international news and current affairs that places people at the heart of the story, rooted in the belief that everyone has a story worth hearing. Through its fearless journalism and renown programming, it tells authentic stories about people everywhere, without geographical or cultural prejudice.

The Program Editor will be responsible for producing news programmes consistent with Al Jazeera’s commitment to accuracy, balance and quality production. You will decide the editorial lines of the day and how stories should be developed and presented and be responsible for outputting live news shows from the gallery.

title: Two Years Ago, Meta Killed CrowdTangle. Can a New AI Tool Fill the Void?
content:
In 2024, Meta shuttered CrowdTangle, a tool used to track how content spread across Facebook and Instagram. The portal was an essential tool for journalists, fact-checkers, and researchers, who used it for more than a decade to monitor viral content — and the spread of misinformation.

CrowdTangle’s end came slowly. Meta disinvested in the tool over years by cutting funding, disbanding teams, and restricting users. When the company finally announced in March 2024 that CrowdTangle would cease operations in August, a petition signed by more than 100 social media watchdog groups and others warned that, as a result, “almost all outside efforts to identify and prevent political disinformation, incitements to violence, and online harassment of women and minorities will be silenced.”

title: Journalists in Africa and South America Are Mapping the Mines Devouring the World’s Rainforests
content:
In the Amazon and Congo rainforests, investigative journalists are using satellite imagery and artificial intelligence (AI) to expose groups that operate in secret, extracting gold and minerals from some of the world’s most remote regions.

In the Amazon, journalists have mapped thousands of sites where armed groups are clearing forests to mine gold. In the Congo, journalists are identifying areas where artisanal miners use buckets and shovels to illegally extract cobalt and copper.

The projects are on separate continents but face similar challenges: limited resources, dangerous terrain and powerful interests that want to keep their activities hidden. Now, journalists working with the Amazon Mining Watch and Africa Mining Watch projects are sharing strategies to automate parts of their investigations and build cross-border networks to strengthen their reporting.

title: Russian War Recruitment in Africa, Hidden West Bank Settlement Funding, Scams in Southeast Asia, and More: 2026 DIG Awards Shortlist
content:
From September 23 – 27, 2026, the 12th edition of the DIG Festival — Europe’s premier multimedia investigative journalism festival — will showcase a powerhouse lineup of outstanding investigative documentaries and podcasts for attendees in Modena, Italy.

These include the screening of 25 new investigative films — chosen from 300 entries — which will be evaluated by an international jury across five video categories for the annual DIG Awards. The diverse finalists reflect the theme of the 2026 event, “Bella Ciao,” which has emerged as a call to arms for free speech and democracy and recalls a World War II-era protest anthem.

The DIG jury, chaired this year by award-winning Croatian filmmaker Igor Bezinović, will also select winners from among five shortlisted investigative podcasts that tackle harms including systematic exploitation, corruption, and abuse.

title: ‘Once Someone Opens the Door, I Have a Shot’: Colombia’s Ricardo Calderón on His Career Conducting High-Risk Investigations
content: The poster depicting a fountain pen emerging from the barrel of a revolver hung for many years behind Ricardo Calderón’s desk. It was an old cover from Le Nouvel Observateur, and the text above the image read: “Le pouvoir des journalistes,” the power of journalists. A colleague had bought it from a Paris flea market and brought it to the newsroom of Semana magazine in Bogotá, where Calderón worked for more than two decades as an investigative reporter. He loved the poster so much that he made a copy of it so he could see it every morning when he walked into his office.
